name: Mabuterol
lead: Mabuterol is a selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist developed as an oral bronchodilator for asthma, chemically related to clenbuterol [1][2]. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding discussion it is grouped with clenbuterol-type compounds that people associate with fat loss and a leaner, more defined physique.

Published human research dates from the 1980s and 1990 and concerns asthma, not body composition. A dose-finding study in 245 asthmatic patients identified 50 micrograms as the optimal single dose, and a 6-week comparison supported 50 micrograms twice daily [2]. A small crossover trial compared it with clenbuterol and fenoterol on early-morning breathing dips [3].
It is not a mainstream marketed drug. Mabuterol appears mostly in analytical chemistry papers that screen for beta-agonist residues in livestock and feed [4].

chain: Selective beta-2 agonist related to clenbuterol
Beta-agonists are associated with raised metabolism and heart-rate effects
Used in hopes of a leaner physique
angle.text: Users group mabuterol with clenbuterol-like compounds sought for cutting body fat. Human studies of it concern asthma, and none have examined fat loss.

card.summary: A clenbuterol-like beta-2 agonist bronchodilator that is discussed as an alternative for cutting body fat and getting leaner.
card.note: Beta-agonists can cause palpitations and tremor; no fat-loss studies exist.

quick.overview:
Mabuterol is a beta-2 agonist originally studied as a tablet for asthma. It is a close chemical relative of clenbuterol.

In physique communities it is mentioned as a clenbuterol-type compound for cutting. It is rarely seen on the market and mostly turns up in drug-residue testing literature.
quick.mechanism: It activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, relaxing airway smooth muscle, and in animal work was more potent than isoprenaline and salbutamol at relaxing guinea pig trachea [5]. Beta-agonist class effects in the body include increased heart rate.
quick.risks: Clinical studies reported good tolerability at 40-60 micrograms in asthma patients [1]. Related drugs caused palpitations in a comparison trial [3]. Animal toxicology studies reported irritability and salivation at high doses [6]. It is not an approved product in major markets.

infobox: Not a marketed approved drug in major markets

sections.h: Use in appearance and body-composition communities
paras: The chain people have in mind runs from beta-2 receptor stimulation, to a raised metabolic rate and fat mobilisation, to a leaner, more defined physique during a "cut". Mabuterol is discussed as a relative of clenbuterol, the best-known compound of this type, which Wikipedia describes as popular in bodybuilding cutting phases and credits Dan Duchaine with popularising in that community.[14][1]

Clenbuterol is described as more potent and longer-acting than salbutamol, with high oral bioavailability and an elimination half-life of 36 to 48 hours; its reported adverse effects include nervousness, tachycardia, raised blood pressure and, with misuse, palpitations.[14] Mabuterol's own human data are limited to 1980s and 1990 asthma studies, so the clenbuterol profile is a reference point for the class rather than a description of mabuterol.[2][3]

Mabuterol relaxed isolated guinea pig tracheal muscle more potently than isoprenaline and salbutamol in laboratory comparisons [5]. A cardiovascular study in animals reported lowered blood pressure and a slight heart-rate rise at low intravenous doses [7]. In rats it showed enantioselective kinetics, with slow absorption and a longer half-life for the R form [8].

A study on isolated, blood-perfused dog right atrium examined beta-adrenoceptor blocking effects of mabuterol, indicating that the compound can interact with receptors in cardiac tissue as well as in airway muscle [10]. In the original pharmacology series, mabuterol was compared with isoprenaline, salbutamol and procaterol, and its relaxing effect on guinea pig trachea was inhibited by beta-blocking agents, which pointed to beta-receptor activation as its mechanism [5].

Beta-2 agonists as a class relax airway smooth muscle through the beta-2 adrenergic receptor. Cardiac tissue also carries beta receptors, which is why the heart-rate and blood-pressure effects seen in the animal series are tracked in studies of these compounds.[7][10]

An open pilot of 10 patients with reversible obstructive lung disease found a useful bronchodilating effect at 40 and 60 micrograms with good tolerability [1]. A summary of first studies covered 245 asthma patients in dose-finding and a multicenter 6-week comparison [2]. A randomized crossover study in 10 patients with nocturnal asthma compared it with clenbuterol and fenoterol; all three reduced morning dipping in some lung measures [3]. No studies have examined mabuterol for fat loss or body composition.

In the pilot study, airway resistance, thoracic gas volume, pulse rate and blood pressure were measured after oral doses of 40, 60 and 80 micrograms, with 0.4 mg inhaled fenoterol as a comparator [1]. In the nocturnal asthma crossover, each of ten patients received no drug on a control night and then 50 micrograms of mabuterol, 40 micrograms of clenbuterol and 5 mg of fenoterol on separate nights. Clenbuterol significantly inhibited the morning dip across several lung-function measures, while mabuterol and fenoterol did so for forced vital capacity and FEV1; palpitations were reported by two subjects after clenbuterol, and the authors noted that the effects varied between drugs [3].

Acute, subacute and chronic toxicity studies in mice, rats, rabbits and dogs reported dose-dependent irritability and hypersalivation in rats at 10 mg/kg and above, with deaths at the highest dose [6].

A 2023 paper described a mabuterol transdermal patch intended for asthma. The authors paired the drug with lactic acid as a counter-ion and tested adhesives to overcome the compound's thermal instability, reporting that the ion-pair formulation retained about 15% more drug content than a plain patch after 12 months at room temperature [11].

Mabuterol is one of a group of beta-agonists that residue-testing laboratories screen for in livestock. Published liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry methods list it with clenbuterol, ractopamine, salbutamol and others for detection in swine urine, bovine urine, animal feed and drinking water [4][12][13].

In six rats given a single oral dose of the racemate, both enantiomers were absorbed slowly, with peak concentrations after roughly 5 to 6 hours. R-mabuterol had a higher exposure and a longer half-life (14.5 hours) than S-mabuterol (9.6 hours) [8].
Mabuterol is 1-[4-amino-3-chloro-5-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]-2-(tert-butylamino)ethanol, with molar mass about 310.75 g/mol; patents date to the 1970s [9].

Wikipedia lists mabuterol with clenbuterol and cimaterol as related aminophenyl ethanolamines. Patents for the compound class date to 1974, assigned to German firms including Thomae and Boehringer, and a 1984 synthesis paper and a 1984 Japanese pharmacology series described the compound as a new selective beta-2 stimulant.[9] The synthesis described there runs to ten steps and ends with reduction of a ketone with sodium borohydride.[9]
It is mentioned alongside clenbuterol-like beta-agonists for cutting. Analytical papers list it among beta-agonists screened for in animal feed and urine [4].

Mabuterol has no marketed pharmaceutical product in major markets and Wikipedia lists no legal status or ATC code for it.[9] In sport, WADA's prohibited list classes clenbuterol as an anabolic agent; mabuterol is likewise a beta-2 agonist that residue-testing laboratories monitor in livestock feed and urine.[14][4] Mentions in appearance forums are largely by association with clenbuterol rather than reports of use.
